Evelyn / team —

Quick technical pass on the deliverables. I've updated the diagram (attached) and drafted the 3–5 bullet threat-path summary below. Notes inline where I think Orion will want clarifying language.

1) Deployment separation model (key points):
- Customer workloads run in customer-managed VPC/subnet (Private mode) or in dedicated Redwood GPU pool separated by tenant isolation namespaces (Dedicated).
- Control plane (Redwood management APIs, billing telemetry) is offered as a logically separate plane; in Private deployments the control plane communicates over customer-configured private link or mTLS-protected egress with attestations.
- Management/patching channels are constrained to limited maintenance windows and authenticated via customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) where requested.
- KV caches and inference-only kernels are ephemerally loaded per-inference host; no persistent model weights are written to shared customer storage in hosted/dedicated flows.

2) Short threat-path summary (most probable vectors + mitigations):
- Misconfigured network ACLs permitting lateral movement from customer tenant subnets to management interfaces. Mitigation: default-deny egress for tenant subnets; allowlist management control-plane CIDRs and require mutual TLS for all management connections.
- Compromised model artifacts or weights via supply-chain or pipeline attack. Mitigation: signed model artifacts, reproducible build hashes, runtime integrity checks, and strict artifact registry access control (read-only for inference nodes).
- KV-cache side-channel leakage when multi-tenant hardware is used. Mitigation: preferred: dedicated capacity for high-risk tenants; otherwise strict cache partitioning, periodic cache flush on tenant boundary, and quantization-friendly isolation kernels.
- Unauthorized API access via stale credentials or long-lived tokens. Mitigation: short-lived tokens, rotation automation, and request tracing that ties token use to session and IP ranges.
- Privileged remote management sessions abused during maintenance windows. Mitigation: customer-scheduled maintenance windows, session recording, ephemeral bastion credentials, and attestation logs in audit stream.

3) Recommended artifacts to include in RFP appendix: diagram (attached), segmentation matrix (attached), and a one-page contract-friendly isolation blurb we can provide. Also recommend requesting a SOC2/ISO snapshot and a list of supported KMS/HSM integrations if required.

Attachments: rdw-threat-path-onepager.pdf (draft), deployment-seg-diagram-v2.png (updated), segmentation-matrix.xlsx (updated)

I'll flag anything in the diagram that needs legal review.

—Vivek
VP, Applied Infra & Inference
Redwood Inference
